title: LEUKODYSTROPHY, ADULT-ONSET, AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT, WITHOUT AMYLOID ANGIOPATHY

intro.text: This entry describes an adult-onset, autosomal dominant leukodystrophy in which, unlike related hereditary cerebral amyloid angiopathies, amyloid angiopathy is not present. The causal gene and the primary reports are not given here because they cannot be recalled reliably.

checks.claim: Adult-onset autosomal dominant leukodystrophy without amyloid angiopathy is a leukodystrophy that begins in adulthood.
checks.evidence_quote: We describe a novel adult onset leukodystrophy in 16 patients from eight families

checks.claim: Adult-onset autosomal dominant leukodystrophy without amyloid angiopathy is inherited as an autosomal dominant trait.
checks.evidence_quote: carrying one of four different stop-gain or frameshift dominant variants in the CST3 gene
checks.explanation: The abstract describes dominant variants in the autosomal gene CST3 across eight families. 'Autosomal' is standard nomenclature.

checks.claim: In adult-onset autosomal dominant leukodystrophy without amyloid angiopathy, unlike in related hereditary cerebral amyloid angiopathies, amyloid angiopathy is not present.
checks.evidence_quote: Histopathologic characterization in two autopsy cases did not reveal angiopathy, but instead micro- to macrocystic degeneration of the white matter.
checks.explanation: The title ('without amyloid angiopathy') and the contrast with Icelandic cerebral amyloid angiopathy support this.

paragraphs.text: Adult-onset autosomal dominant leukodystrophy without amyloid angiopathy (ADLDWA) is a neurodegenerative disorder of cerebral white matter. It begins in adulthood and is passed on as an autosomal dominant trait. Brain imaging shows leukoencephalopathy. The name sets it apart from hereditary cerebral amyloid angiopathies with white matter involvement, because no amyloid angiopathy is found.

checks.claim: Adult-onset autosomal dominant leukodystrophy without amyloid angiopathy (ADLDWA) is a neurodegenerative disorder of cerebral white matter.
checks.evidence_quote: Histopathologic characterization in two autopsy cases did not reveal angiopathy, but instead micro- to macrocystic degeneration of the white matter.
checks.explanation: Describes a degenerative leukodystrophy of the cerebral white matter with progressive motor and cognitive decline.

checks.claim: Brain imaging in adult-onset autosomal dominant leukodystrophy without amyloid angiopathy (ADLDWA) shows leukoencephalopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: Radiologically, pathognomonic changes are found at typical predilection sites involving the deep cerebral white matter sparing a periventricular and directly subcortical rim
checks.explanation: Imaging shows white matter changes, i.e. leukoencephalopathy.

checks.claim: No amyloid angiopathy is found in adult-onset autosomal dominant leukodystrophy without amyloid angiopathy (ADLDWA), which sets it apart from hereditary cerebral amyloid angiopathies with white matter involvement.
checks.evidence_quote: Clinical and radiological features differ markedly from the previously described Icelandic cerebral amyloid angiopathy found in patients carrying p.Leu68Asn substitution in CST3.
checks.explanation: Together with the title and the autopsy finding of no angiopathy, this supports the distinction from hereditary cerebral amyloid angiopathy.

paragraphs.text: As the name states, the disorder is passed on as an autosomal dominant trait.
